plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single-trace ultraviolet absorption spectrum of 1,3-butadiene plotted over a pink gradient field. The vertical axis is labeled "Absorbance", carries a magenta arrow pointing up beside the label, and runs from 0 to 1.0 with labeled ticks every 0.2. The horizontal axis reads "Wavelength (nm)", is followed by a magenta arrow pointing right, and spans 200 to 400 with labeled ticks every 20 nm. One magenta curve enters at the left edge near 0.34, climbs steeply to a rounded maximum just under 0.9 at about 215 nm, then falls sharply through 240 nm to roughly 0.07, after which it declines almost imperceptibly along a near-horizontal tail to about 0.03 at the right edge. A short annotation just above and right of the crest reads "lambda max = 217 nm". With the zero baseline at the bottom of the chart rather than the top, absorption registers as a peak rising off a flat floor, and the eye is meant to fix on that lone crest against the featureless tail beyond 250 nm. The trace records the wavelength of strongest absorption for a simple conjugated diene, the reading from which molar absorptivity is calculated.

interactionPlan.concept: The UV spectrum of 1,3-butadiene shows a single strong absorption maximum near 217 nm, the λmax used to characterize a conjugated π system and to compute molar absorptivity.

Plot area filled with a soft pink vertical gradient (deeper pink at the top fading to white at the bottom)

Single magenta absorption curve for 1,3-butadiene: enters at left near A≈0.34, rises steeply to a rounded crest of A≈0.87 at ~215 nm, drops sharply through 240 nm to A≈0.07, then a near-flat tail declining to A≈0.03 at 400 nm
Text annotation above and right of the crest: 'λmax = 217 nm'

Thin baseline at A = 0 along the bottom of the plot

interactions.teaches: That absorbance is a function of wavelength, and that λmax is simply the wavelength at which that function reaches its single highest value — not a separate property read off elsewhere.
interactions.label: Wavelength (nm)

interactions.teaches: That essentially all of butadiene's diagnostic UV absorption sits in a narrow band near 217 nm, while everything past 250 nm is a featureless, near-zero tail carrying no structural information.
interactions.label: Region emphasis

demo_steps.title: The whole spectrum
demo_steps.narration: Absorbance is plotted against wavelength from 200 to 400 nm. One sharp crest dominates the left edge; the rest of the trace hugs the baseline.

demo_steps.title: Climbing toward the maximum
demo_steps.narration: Drag the marker to 210 nm and the readout climbs fast — absorbance nearly triples over ten nanometers as the π→π* transition comes into resonance.

demo_steps.title: λmax = 217 nm
demo_steps.narration: At the crest the readout reaches its highest value. This single wavelength, λmax, is what is reported for 1,3-butadiene and what is paired with concentration and path length to get molar absorptivity.

demo_steps.title: Falling off the peak
demo_steps.narration: Move past 240 nm and absorbance collapses to below 0.1. The absorption band is narrow: only a small window of wavelengths matches the transition energy.

demo_steps.title: The uninformative tail
demo_steps.narration: Beyond 250 nm the curve is almost flat and almost zero — butadiene is transparent here. A diene with more conjugation would push a peak into this region, which is exactly why the tail is worth watching.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: λmax is not a label added to the picture — it is the single wavelength where the curve peaks, and for a simple conjugated diene like 1,3-butadiene that peak sits at 217 nm with essentially nothing above 250 nm.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Wide landscape line plot. Plot area carries a vertical pink gradient, saturated rose at the top fading to near-white at the baseline; axes drawn as thin black lines with black tick labels. A single bright magenta/crimson curve about 2–3 px wide: starts at the left boundary around A=0.34, rises steeply to a smooth rounded maximum just under 0.9 near 215 nm, descends sharply so that by 240 nm it is near 0.07, then a nearly horizontal tail drifting gently down to ~0.03 at 400 nm. Italic serif annotation 'λmax = 217 nm' in black, placed just above and to the right of the crest with no leader line. Magenta arrows: one pointing up to the left of the 'Absorbance' axis title (rotated vertical), one pointing right after 'Wavelength (nm)'. Interactive additions: a filled magenta dot on the curve at the slider wavelength with a faint vertical dropline to the x-axis and a small readout chip showing 'λ = 217 nm, A = 0.87'. Region toggle dims the non-selected wavelength range (reduce curve opacity and grey-wash the gradient there) and draws a soft highlight band behind the selected range.

authoredContext:
Note that UV spectra differ from IR spectra in how they are presented. For historical reasons, IR spectra are usually displayed so that the baseline corresponding to zero absorption runs across the top of the chart and a valley indicates an absorption, whereas UV spectra are displayed with the baseline at the bottom of the chart so that a peak indicates an absorption (the figure).

The ultraviolet spectrum of 1,3-butadiene, λmax = 217 nm.

Background gradient is noticeably more saturated pink at the top and retains pink further down than the source, which fades to near-white by mid-height.

Extra on-plot chrome not in the source: a bordered 'λ = 200 nm  A = 0.34' readout chip in the upper-right, a magenta marker dot, and a dashed dropline to the axis (justifiable as interactive affordances but they change the default appearance).
The source curve's apex sits slightly left of the 220 tick (~215 nm) with a gentle rounded crest; the generated crest is sharper and the left flank rises more abruptly from the 200 nm edge value.
Y-axis title 'Absorbance' is placed lower on the axis than in the source (centered near the lower third) and the up-arrow sits closer to the label, slightly changing the left-margin composition.
evaluation.notes: Faithful reproduction of the butadiene UV spectrum with correct axes, ticks, pink gradient fill, arrowed axis titles and the λmax = 217 nm annotation, plus a genuinely useful set of interactions (wavelength scrub, region emphasis, λmax jump, 5-step demo, click explainers); main weaknesses are the squeezed near-square plot aspect that turns the band into a spike, a slightly over-saturated gradient, and extra on-plot readout chrome absent from the source.

Soften the background gradient so it fades to essentially white by ~40% of the plot height, matching the source's lighter lower half.
Make the readout chip, marker dot and dashed dropline appear only after the user interacts (or render them much more subtly) so the step-0 state matches the static source image.
Slightly broaden the left flank / shift the apex toward ~215 nm and reduce the steepness near 200 nm so the crest shape matches the source trace.
